name: Transient Neonatal Multiple Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency
aliases: Transient Neonatal Glutaric Aciduria Type II

criteria.description: Neonatal onset of metabolic acidosis with hypoglycemia and hypotonia
Elevated plasma acylcarnitines and urinary organic acids consistent with multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
Reduced activity of multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenases in fibroblasts or leukocytes
Identification of pathogenic variants in ETFA, ETFB, or ETFDH genes (supportive but not always present)
Spontaneous clinical and biochemical recovery within weeks to months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neonatal metabolic acidosis with characteristic biochemical markers and reduced enzyme activity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is supportive but not mandatory due to transient nature

searchTerms: high acid levels in newborn metabolism
low blood sugar in newborn period

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypotonia presenting in the neonatal period
searchTerms: low muscle tone starting in newborn period
poor sucking or swallowing in neonates

laboratory: Increased urinary glutaric, ethylmalonic, and other organic acids
imaging: Normal or transient mild hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
Possible cardiomegaly on chest X-ray if cardiomyopathy present
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ETFA, ETFB, or ETFDH genes associated with MADD
Transient neonatal form may lack identifiable mutations
other: Reduced activity of multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenases in fibroblast or leukocyte assays
Spontaneous clinical and biochemical resolution within weeks to months

distinguishingFeatures: Persistent metabolic abnormalities without spontaneous resolution
More severe clinical course with progressive neuromuscular symptoms
Different metabolic profiles on urine organic acid analysis

redFlags: Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to treatment
Progressive hypotonia and encephalopathy beyond neonatal period
Failure to thrive or persistent hypoglycemia
references: Roe CR, et al. Transient neonatal multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: clinical and biochemical features. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2000;23(3):215-223.
